slots.title: U.S. cash session — Sept. 9, 2026
slots.body:
The S&P 500 finished at 7,637.70, down 35.82 points (-0.5%) after an intraday range of 7,624.16–7,660.68.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 405.41 points (-0.8%) to 52,380.66, the largest index decline in the set by percentage among the three main U.S. benchmarks.

The Nasdaq Composite closed at 26,256.66 (-0.6%, -164.76 points).
The Russell 2000 was -1.3% at 2,921.23, underperforming the large-cap indexes in the injected close data.

The VIX rose 4.7% to 16.46 (prior close 15.72), the only major U.S. index-style reading in the bundle that finished higher on the day.

Sector averages on Nasdaq for Sept. 9 showed Industrials weakest at -2.0%, Energy at -1.2%, Financial Services at -1.0%, and Utilities at -0.8%.
Technology was +0.5% and Healthcare +0.2%; Communication Services +0.2%.
That mix fits a session where one megacap advancer offset broader tech softness elsewhere.

Meta ($META) closed +6.6% at 653.69 (+40.21 from the prior close).
Alphabet ($GOOG) was -2.1% at 328.38, Amazon ($AMZN) -1.8% at 252.40, and UnitedHealth ($UNH) -1.9% at 393.06 with a wide session range down to 378.08 in the quote data.

Chewy ($CHWY) reported EPS 0.20 versus estimate 0.178 and revenue about $3.33B versus estimate ~$3.32B, yet the stock finished -10.8% at 20.75.
Cooper Companies ($COO) posted EPS 1.15 vs 1.12 estimate but revenue below estimate and closed -6.2% at 63.48.
Sunbelt Rentals ($SUNB) beat on EPS (1.18 vs 1.04) and revenue and finished +5.9% at 73.42.

ServiceTitan ($TTAN) was among the steepest liquid declines at -30.0% to 57.12 in the losers screen.
Signet ($SIG) was +23.9% at 102.41 among liquid gainers.
AeroVironment ($AVAV) reported EPS 0.59 vs 0.22 estimate and still closed -5.4% at 140.80.

On the calendar, the MBA 30-year mortgage rate printed 6.8% (previous 6.8%), mortgage applications -2.7%, and Redbook year-over-year retail sales tracker 8.3% (previous 9.6%).
The 10-year note auction cleared at 4.8% in the economic calendar entry; the treasury snapshot in the data shows a 10-year yield of 4.8% dated 2026-09-04 with 2s10s spread 0.41.
Coverage tied the session tone to oil strength and bond-market reaction after Treasury buyback details — see the linked Barron’s and WSJ pieces in the news feed.

Cross-asset: gold futures (GCUSD) were essentially flat at 4,462.90 (0.0%).
The United States Oil Fund ($USO proxy in data) was +2.7% at 149.97; Brent (BZUSD) -0.3% at 100.91.
The dollar fund proxy (UUP) was flat at 27.98.
Bitcoin (BTCUSD) +0.2% at 78,433.29.

Overseas indexes in the bundle were lower: FTSE 100 -1.3%, Hang Seng -1.4%, Nikkei 225 -0.8%, and the Germany ETF proxy (EWG) -1.2%.
